ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Temporary discoloration

An otherwise well adult notices a dark tongue and darker stools after short-term bismuth subsalicylate use. He has no dizziness, abdominal pain, tarry stool or bleeding symptoms. Which medication effect can explain these temporary changes?

  1. Iron deficiency caused by one dose
  2. Bismuth-related dark discoloration
  3. Guaranteed gastrointestinal hemorrhage in every user
  4. Permanent destruction of tongue tissue
  5. A specific diagnostic sign of liver failure
Answer and explanation

Bismuth-related dark discoloration

Bismuth can temporarily darken the tongue and stool; concerning bleeding symptoms still need assessment.

Option explanations

Bismuth-related dark discoloration: Bismuth can temporarily darken the tongue and stool; concerning bleeding symptoms still need assessment.

Guaranteed gastrointestinal hemorrhage in every user: The medication can cause benign discoloration, although bleeding must not be ignored when suspected.

Permanent destruction of tongue tissue: The usual discoloration is temporary.

A specific diagnostic sign of liver failure: Darkening alone does not diagnose hepatic failure.

Iron deficiency caused by one dose: This does not explain the rapid tongue discoloration.
